capabilities.title: Architecture and composition
capabilities.summary: Lifecycle-aware Model, System, Utility, Controller, installer, command, query, and event composition.
capabilities.boundary: Use roles for ownership and lifecycle, not as mandatory wrappers for every class.

capabilities.title: Async lifecycle and cancellation
capabilities.summary: Owned completion, cancellation scopes, signal waits, retries, progress, gates, and bounded aggregation.
capabilities.boundary: The caller owns business retries and rollback; GF owns reusable terminal-state and cancellation mechanics.

capabilities.title: Assets, resource identity, and content
capabilities.summary: Async resource handles, stable resource keys, catalogs, preload plans, optional content packages, and auditable generated-artifact export plans.
capabilities.boundary: Projects define content taxonomy, materialization, target adapters, and distribution policy; GF provides identity, lifecycle, plans, and diagnostics.

capabilities.title: Configuration and data pipelines
capabilities.summary: Runtime config resources plus staged, validated, versioned-IR table compilation at build time.
capabilities.boundary: Business columns and schemas belong to project inputs; reusable reading, validation, target, and commit mechanics belong to the tool.

capabilities.title: Versioned analytics events and durable handoff
capabilities.summary: Exact event-name and schema-version validation, structured tracking reports, and provider-neutral handoff to a dedicated persistent request outbox.
capabilities.boundary: GF validates the declared properties contract and coordinates an at-least-once queue handoff. Projects own event taxonomy, explicit version migration, PII and consent policy, authentication, replay authorization, retention, and server-side idempotency.

capabilities.title: Storage, save graphs, and migration
capabilities.summary: Local storage codecs, backend synchronization, slot metadata, scene save graphs, transactional save profiles, rollback, recovery, identity, and explicit migration.
capabilities.boundary: Projects own save fields, compatibility guarantees, conflict policy, and cloud provider adapters.

capabilities.title: Input mapping and rebinding
capabilities.summary: Abstract actions, contexts, modifiers, triggers, recording, conflict analysis, rebinding, touch, and drag/drop mechanisms.
capabilities.boundary: GF maps intent; projects define action names, UI, accessibility policy, and gameplay meaning.

capabilities.title: UI state, binding, and navigation
capabilities.summary: Layered UI navigation, screen state, reactive binding, repeaters, transitions, and focus-friendly project composition.
capabilities.boundary: GF owns navigation and binding mechanics; projects own visual hierarchy, copy, and product flows.

capabilities.title: Scalable and virtualized UI collections
capabilities.summary: Bounded virtual-list materialization, stable item identity and focus, transactional table predicates, repeater binding, and large collection presentation.
capabilities.boundary: GF owns bounded visible windows, recycler lifecycle, focus projection, and transactional predicate execution; projects own authoritative data and identity, domain predicate construction, row visuals, input, accessibility, and product semantics.

capabilities.title: Audio playback and backend adaptation
capabilities.summary: Audio clips, typed playback regions and loop points, banks, events, pooled emitters, buses, beat clocks, and optional middleware backends.
capabilities.boundary: GF accepts only playback regions that the selected stream or backend can express exactly and never simulates bounded ends by polling. Middleware SDK calls belong in a backend adapter; projects own event naming and mix policy.

capabilities.title: Render preparation and multimodal feedback
capabilities.summary: Shader parameters, render warmup, screen transitions, haptics, and shake mechanisms for project-owned visual and tactile feedback.
capabilities.boundary: GF owns reusable parameter application, warmup, transition, haptic, and shake lifecycles; projects own effect meaning, timing, budgets, art direction, accessibility policy, and static fallbacks.

capabilities.title: State machines and flow orchestration
capabilities.summary: Node and resource state machines, flow graphs, action queues, behavior trees, and decision mechanisms.
capabilities.boundary: Select one mechanism by state ownership and observability; do not layer several orchestrators without a distinct responsibility.

capabilities.title: Undo, redo, and command history
capabilities.summary: Undoable commands, bounded undo and redo stacks, snapshots, serialization, restoration, and failure-aware synchronous or asynchronous history transitions.
capabilities.boundary: GF owns bounded history stacks, invocation ordering, signal-completion waits, terminal-success hooks, and atomic cursor preservation when a transition fails; projects own command semantics, terminal-success policy, snapshot schemas, domain preconditions, restore atomicity, persistence policy, and business validation.

capabilities.title: Bounded runtime work and object reuse
capabilities.summary: Explicit execution budgets and reusable object pools for keeping analysis, effects, and other bursty runtime work bounded.
capabilities.boundary: GF supplies explicit budget checks and reusable pool lifecycle mechanics; projects must profile first and own capacity, frame priority, exhaustion behavior, reset semantics, and authoritative domain identity.

capabilities.title: Diagnostics, logs, support, and operations
capabilities.summary: Structured logs, bounded lazy diagnostic providers, headless health evidence, operation timelines, session traces, debug surfaces, support reports, and build metadata.
capabilities.boundary: Collect the minimum needed data, bound all histories, and require explicit consent for precise or private diagnostics.

capabilities.title: Runtime Agent endpoint environment
capabilities.summary: Default-closed, transport-neutral runtime endpoints with strict JSON schemas, exact short-lived grants, replay and rate controls, policy checks, bounded responses, and payload-free audit.
capabilities.boundary: GF protects untrusted request data entering trusted synchronous handlers. Create the environment on its long-lived owner thread, marshal every transport call back to that thread, and call invalidate_policy_context before mutating registry, provider, or external policy state. Projects still own pre-decode body limits, transport authentication and throttling, user approval, business authorization, side-effect rollback, and process isolation.

capabilities.title: Deterministic data and simulation primitives
capabilities.summary: Fixed random sequences, canonical Variant serialization, seeds, tick histories, and explicit deterministic scopes.
capabilities.boundary: Declare the deterministic scope and numeric contract; do not assume all Godot values or physics are cross-platform deterministic.

capabilities.title: Network transport and contracts
capabilities.summary: Replaceable byte transports, adoptable MultiplayerPeer bridges, typed lobby operations, transport metrics, snapshots, histories, and bounded authoritative synchronization with optional prediction correction.
capabilities.boundary: GF can coordinate a bounded full-snapshot authority flow, but the project chooses trusted authority identity, entity control, state and input schemas, business conflict policy, matchmaking, lobby policy, and provider identity.

capabilities.title: Platform and SDK adapters
capabilities.summary: Contract-described project-owned translation boundaries for identity, lobby, activation intents, storage, achievements, social, lifecycle, payment, and other provider capabilities.
capabilities.boundary: Provider code is a separate adapter. Only stable provider-neutral contracts are candidates for GF.

capabilities.title: Reusable domain components
capabilities.summary: Generic inventory, attributes, traits, equipment, quests, level catalogs, interactions, combat, and turn-based primitives.
capabilities.boundary: GF components store generic state and mechanisms; game economy, rewards, balance, and content semantics remain project code.

capabilities.title: Dialogue resources and execution
capabilities.summary: Provider-neutral dialogue resources, conditions, mutations, responses, runners, and strict text compilation.
capabilities.boundary: GF does not define character databases, quest side effects, localization storage, UI, or a project-specific script language.

capabilities.title: Spatial math and physics mechanisms
capabilities.summary: Grid/path math, spatial queries, policy-driven bounded 2D canvas orchestration, camera mechanisms, hit detection, buoyancy sampling, and physics-independent policies.
capabilities.boundary: GFSpatialCanvas2D orchestrates view, validated input routing, selection, and placement operation records only; projects own action naming, TileMap or scene mutation, business legality, persistence, UGC, collision layers, world semantics, authority, and force application policy.

capabilities.title: Project layout and authoring tools
capabilities.summary: Optional read-only project layout analysis, explanation, impact simulation, planning, bounded portable-safe profile evaluation, data compilers, editor contributions, and CI validation.
capabilities.boundary: Tools are optional and profile-driven; Project Layout only scans, explains, simulates impact, and produces reviewable plans, never applies project changes or turns one game's directory into a GF runtime requirement. Project profile inventories, audit work, diagnostics, and portable_safe_v1 regexes have non-configurable fail-closed limits shared by their canonical contract.
